preamble: Lowering of the nucleus of [ou]/[ɔu] to [au], parallel to [ei] > [ai]. Middle High German ou (boum, ouge) became New High German au (Baum, Auge), merging with the au that arose from diphthongized ū. In late-20th-century Netherlands Dutch ('Polder Dutch', Stroop 1998) ou in koud, vrouw, jou was lowered and lengthened to [aːu] alongside ei > [ai] and ui > [ʌy].

examples.note: Stroop: the original ou becomes noticeably wider and lower and sounds like aau [aːu]; a Netherlands-only change, absent in Flemish.

sources: Stroop, J. (1998). Poldernederlands: Waardoor het ABN verdwijnt. Bert Bakker. https://www.dbnl.org/tekst/stro008pold01_01/stro008pold01_01_0004.php
